note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. He reports that he has been doing yard work in the last week or so and started to feel really tired, was short of breath. He believes he caught his first cold and it just got worse. He denies any history of seasonal allergies.

The patient reports that he usually feels short of breath when lifting or carrying something. He was doing landscaping, so he was carrying heavy bags of soil and he got really winded. It really surprised him. He denies coughing up anything but feels like that is next. He also denies fevers but thinks it was because he was exerting himself. The patient reports my elbows hurt quite a bit and his knees were pretty tired. He thinks that was a lot to do with lifting the bags.

In terms of his other medical problems, the patient reports that it has been kind of a crazy year and a half. He was a little concerned about that but for the most part has been doing well with it. His wife got him into barre classes to help him relax and she thinks it is working.

The patient reports that he has been monitoring his sugar levels while he is going to work during the week but not on weekends. The diet has been pretty good for the most part except for some house parties and things like that. However, he notes that they have not been elevated at all since this episode of his diabetes.

The patient reports that he has been monitoring his blood pressure at home but not on weekends. He notes that it has been under control and is taking his medication as prescribed.

The patient denies any nausea or vomiting or diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers.
• Respiratory: Endorses shortness of breath on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea or vomiting or diarrhea.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with ronchi present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray today in office reviewed in office today shows no airspace disease, no pneumonia.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Upper respiratory infection.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with an upper respiratory infection which I believe is viral in nature given his symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including over-the-counter cough medication (Robitussin) and antipyretics (Tylenol). I advised him to follow up if symptoms worsen.
- Medical Treatment: We will send a COVID-19 test to rule out COVID-19 as well as send him home with Robitussin for cough relief and Tylenol for fever relief.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with symptoms consistent with depression which have improved significantly since starting barre classes at home.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including psychotherapy referral if needed in addition to continuing barre classes at home if desired by the patient at this time in 3 months we will check on this further.
- Medical Treatment: Continue barre classes at home if desired by the patient at this time in 3 months we will check on this further; refer to psychotherapy if needed at this time.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus uncontrolled.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus which is elevated hemoglobin A1c level of 8%. This indicates poor glucose control over time which can lead to complications such as heart disease, kidney disease, nerve damage, etc.,
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including increasing metformin dose from 1000 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily; we will order another hemoglobin A1c in 4 months to monitor progress; dietary advice was also provided as well as encouragement to continue monitoring blood glucose levels while at work but not on weekends.
- Medical Treatment: Increase metformin dose from 1000 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily; order hemoglobin A1c in 4 months.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam. She has been walking, exercising, and doing yoga, which has helped with her arthritis a lot. She has not had any joint pain recently. She is still taking methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly without any issues. Her atrial fibrillation symptoms have not improved with stress management techniques such as meditation and running with her dog. She has noticed that her palpitations start to flare up again when she starts to get stressed. She was placed on Protonix 40 mg daily and dietary modifications have helped reduce her symptoms of reflux. She has not had a flare up in over 5 months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses palpitations.
• Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.
• Gastrointestinal: Endorses dyspepsia.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm at this time. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, which we've heard in the past so I'm not worried at that.
• Respiratory: Lungs are nice and clear.
• Musculoskeletal: Right elbow shows edema and erythema. Pain to palpation of the right elbow.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Event monitor results show that she is in and out of atrial fibrillation, with what we call a conversion pause. We will discuss this further today.
Autoimmune panel shows that everything looks good, it looks like she is well controlled with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: Her current methotrexate prescription appears to be effective in controlling her symptoms at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as prescribed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as prescribed. If she needs a referral back to see the rheumatologist, let me know but I think everything seems stable now.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
2. Atrial Fibrillation.
- Medical Reasoning: Given that she is going in and out of atrial fibrillation, I believe we should keep her in normal sinus rhythm at this point in time due to her age and overall health status.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of avoiding stress triggers such as caffeine or alcohol when experiencing palpitations.
- Medical Treatment: Refer for cardiac ablation which will map out where the rhythm is coming from and burn it so it does not come back.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
3. Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
- Medical Reasoning: Her current protonix prescription appears to be effective in controlling her symptoms at this time, along with dietary modifications which have also been helpful in reducing symptoms of GERD.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on protonix 40 mg daily as prescribed along with dietary modifications such as avoiding coffee or spicy foods, etc., if she experiences any issues with these medications or dietary modifications please contact us immediately.
- Medical Treatment: Continue protonix 40 mg daily as prescribed along with dietary modifications such as avoiding coffee or spicy foods, etc., if she experiences any issues with these medications or dietary modifications please contact us immediately.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hyperglycemia.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and kidney transplant. He is here today for emergency room follow-up.

The patient was seen in the emergency room over the weekend due to elevated blood sugar. He was not staying on top of his blood sugar readings and felt woozy. His wife took him in for evaluation and he was treated as an outpatient.

The patient reports that he has been having difficulty monitoring his diet due to being busy with work and social activities. He has been eating fast food on the weekends. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his kidney transplant, taking immunotherapy medications as prescribed by Dr. Reyes. His last visit with Dr. Reyes was 3 weeks ago, and everything seemed to be fine at that time.

Regarding his depression, the patient reports that it has been about a year-and-a-half or so, but he has been pretty good with it. He notes that he finds relaxation in meditation and would like to continue this for a couple more months to see how it goes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Neurological: Denies dizziness or lightheadedness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation; no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi present.
• Cardiovascular: Carotid bruits are absent bilaterally; grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur present over the left sternal border; no gallops, rubs, or murmurs present elsewhere.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: 8%.
Fasting Glucose: 162.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Hyperglycemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated blood glucose levels are likely due to poor dietary habits and lack of monitoring of blood glucose levels.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications and the importance of monitoring blood glucose levels regularly.
- Medical Treatment: Increase Lantus insulin to 20 units at night; order hemoglobin A1c in a couple months.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well with current strategies with meditation; we will hold off on medication or therapy at this time until further evaluation is completed by me in a couple months if needed.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed current coping mechanisms for managing depression and encouraged him to continue meditation as a healthy coping mechanism until further evaluation is completed by me in a couple months if needed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current coping mechanisms until further evaluation is completed by me in a couple months if needed; call me if needed for any reason at this time.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan at this time until further evaluation is completed by me in a couple months if needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Nguyen is a 54-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for osteoporosis and multiple sclerosis who presents for an annual exam. He has been traveling all over the country. It's been kind of a stressful summer. He is adjusting to everything in the fall and so far it's been good, but he is having trouble sleeping. He has tried everything from melatonin to meditation to stretching out every morning when he gets up. Nothing seems to help.

In terms of his osteoporosis, he is taking Fosamax 1 tab per week. He denies any issues with his joints or any issues like broken bones recently.

In terms of his multiple sclerosis, he last saw the neurologist 6 months ago. He is taking the medication and denies any issues with that. He does have a lingering issue with his right leg from his knee surgery, but other than that it's been fine.

He endorses insomnia and denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or any other issues.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Neurological: Endorses insomnia.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or swelling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Clear bilaterally to auscultation.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs or gallops.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee shows changes from arthritis but otherwise appears good.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Osteoporosis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well on Fosamax 1 tab per week and has not had any recent issues with his joints.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on Fosamax 1 tab per week as prescribed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue on Fosamax 1 tab per week as prescribed. Order a refill of fosamax 1 tab per week, 11 refills.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Lawrence Walker is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux. He presents with complaints of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 10 days ago. He has noticed swelling in his legs. He is uncomfortable when he wakes up in the morning and feels stiff. It takes him a little while to adjust to walking when he gets up. He has not woken up acutely short of breath at night since one episode approximately 1 week ago.

Regarding his diabetes, he is doing well on the insulin pump and has not noticed any spike in his blood sugars recently. He does admit to consuming chocolate bars regularly.

He has been trying natural solutions for his depression, including stretching outdoors every morning during the summer months. However, he is not ready to try any medications yet and is open to suggestions.

He was previously prescribed omeprazole 20 mg daily for reflux and has been making lifestyle modifications by cutting back on red bull and caffeine. His alcohol intake has been challenging during the holiday season but he reports that he is better now.

PAST HISTORY

Type 1 diabetes.
Congestive heart failure.
Depression.
Reflux.

Neck: No jugular venous distension or carotid bruits.

Respiratory: Crackles bilaterally at the bases.
note.objective_results:

Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lawrence Walker is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath today.
1) Acute heart failure exacerbation.
- Medical Reasoning: His symptoms began approximately 10 days ago. He has noticed swelling in his legs. He is uncomfortable when he wakes up in the morning and feels stiff. It takes him a little while to adjust to walking when he gets up. He has not woken up acutely short of breath at night since one episode approximately 1 week ago.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications that may help alleviate his symptoms today in office. I encouraged him to weigh himself daily and contact me if his weight does not decrease or if it increases or if he experiences worsening dyspnea at rest.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Lasix (40 mg/day) for acute heart failure exacerbation today in office.
2) Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood glucose levels have been stable on insulin pump therapy recently but we will order a hemoglobin A1c within the next month to assess if any adjustments are needed at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him to follow up with his endocrinologist as well as schedule a recent eye exam today in office.
- Medical Treatment: We will order a hemoglobin A1c within the next month to assess if any adjustments are needed at this time today in office.
3) Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: He reports that it has been a crazy year and half for him lately and that he has tried natural solutions such as stretching outdoors every morning during the summer months but is not ready to try any medications yet as he is open to suggestions today in office.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him that we will refer him to psychiatry for talk therapy today in office as well as no medication at this time today in office.
4) Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
- Medical Reasoning: His symptoms have improved with omeprazole 20 mg daily but we will continue this medication as prescribed today in office.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder and elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. James is a 64-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of left shoulder and elbow pain. He reports that he has been experiencing constant pain in his left shoulder and left elbow for approximately 5 months, since he fell 5 months ago while going up stairs. He states that he was walking up a flight of stairs to his house when his feet slipped on ice, and he fell on his left side. He believes that his left shoulder and wrist took the brunt of the fall. The patient has been trying to keep up with his usual routine of 2 days per week, but he has had to stop lifting weights due to the pain. He notes that the pain is worse when he lifts, and he has not been able to lift more than 15 or 20 pounds. The patient continues to walk daily with his wife for 30 minutes.

The patient reports that he has tried icing and stopping exercise, which has provided some relief, but the pain still persists.

PAST HISTORY

The patient is a retired office worker.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is married.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he takes no medications.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder and elbow pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without evidence of cervical spine instability or deformity.
Eyes: Extraocular movements are intact bilaterally. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with correction as needed. No signs of strabismus or nystagmus.
Ears, Nose, Mouth and Throat: No signs of infection or inflammation in the ears, nose, mouth or throat.
Respiratory: Auscultation of Lungs reveals clear bilaterally with no wheezes or rales.
Cardiovascular: Auscultation of Heart reveals regular rate with no murmurs or gallops.
Gastrointestinal: No abdominal masses or tenderness noted on examination.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the upper extremities reveals tenderness over the left shoulder and elbow without warmth, erythema or deformity. Positive Hawkins-Kennedy test and Neer's test bilaterally. Normal proximal and distal upper extremity strength. Intact median radial ulnar sensation to light touch bilaterally up to 90 degrees abduction. Empty tan can be tested bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Impingement syndrome of the left shoulder.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with impingement syndrome of the left shoulder after a fall onto an outstretched hand which likely caused an injury to his left shoulder joint capsule leading to impingement syndrome.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today including physical therapy as well as cortisone injections if necessary after physical therapy does not improve symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: We have ordered a referral for Dr. Martha Rivera for physical therapy two days per week at this point in time if symptoms do not improve with physical therapy we will consider cortisone injections as an alternative treatment option.

Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.

note.objective_exam:

Breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female who presents for evaluation of breast reduction. She has been experiencing back pain and neck pain for approximately 5 years, which she believes may be related to her breasts. She has been wearing a 34E sports bra due to discomfort and difficulty finding a regular bra in her size. The patient has not had any children and is currently studying to be a psychologist. She denies any history of tobacco use, alcohol use, or drug use.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing back pain and neck pain for approximately 5 years, which she believes may be related to her breasts. She denies any history of tobacco use, alcohol use, or drug use. The patient reports that she has been going to the chiropractor for a few years due to back pain.

The patient reports that she experiences numbness in her hands and nipple pain on occasion. She denies any rashes underneath her breasts.

The patient reports that certain activities such as working out and running cause her significant pain when holding onto her breasts.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Significant for migraine headaches.
Family History: Mother with prior history of breast cancer at age 40.
Social History: Currently studying to be a psychologist.
Tobacco Use: No prior history.
Alcohol Use: Socially. One glass per week.
Drug Use: No prior history.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Breast Examination:
- Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. There is no nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy is palpable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray measurements reveal a BSA of 2.65 m2.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female who presents for evaluation of breast reduction. She has attempted nonsurgical treatments but minimal relief and is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.
Her minimum required resection based on BSA of 2.65 m2 with Schnur scale is 1,792 grams which should be attainable given her extremely large breasts and the measurements above there is potential for using a nipple graft.
In addition to the surgical procedure we discussed today I have recommended that the patient follow up with me in one week to take photos while she is here so we can submit these to insurance for approval at that time once we have the new provider we will go ahead and get that submitted and then when they approve it we will work with you on a surgery date and then we will meet again right before the surgery to answer any last minute questions and go over the instructions in more detail things like that.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hematuria.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mrs. Kelly Wood is a 41-year-old female who presents for renal ultrasound due to hematuria. The patient reports that she has had bright red urine for the past 6 weeks, and she has had episodes of dysuria and pain with urination. She notes that she passed 2 small stones last week after scheduling this appointment. The patient denies flank pain or lower back tenderness at the present time.

The patient is a chronic urolithiasis patient.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she drinks more Mountain Dew than water.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is taking Alavert 10 mg tablet once daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss, fever, chills, or night sweats.
• Genitourinary: Reports hematuria, dysuria, and pain with urination.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• General Examination: No flank pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Anti-Gu normal vaginal exam.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Urine dipstick: Color yellow and clear, urobilinogen 0.2 EU/dL, pH 5.5 and specific gravity 1.020.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Primary diagnosis: Hematuria.
• Secondary diagnosis: Chronic urolithiasis.
• Medical Reasoning: The blood in her urine was due to kidney stones. Fortunately, she passed two last week and the blood has nearly subsided. She does still have one stone in the left kidney since it's not obstructing or causing pain, I do not recommend any surgical intervention at this time.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the formation of kidney stones can not be attributed to a particular cause but several factors increase the risk such as dehydration, family history, certain foods, digestive tract disease and certain medical conditions. We discussed dietary recommendations to help prevent future kidney stones including drinking half of her body weight in ounces of water per day and avoiding sugary drinks like Mountain Dew. We also discussed foods to avoid such as salty processed food because they are high in sodium and reduce the amount of beef poultry fish pork to less than 1000 mg per day.
• Medical Treatment: Continue Alavert 10 mg tablet once daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Sanchez is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up status post mitral valve repair. She was seen in office on 9/17/2020, at which time we felt that she was doing quite well from a cardiac standpoint, and so we recommended she continue with the same medication.

The patient reports that she is doing well overall. She states that she was having a rough time before surgery, but she thinks she is overall pretty good now though. She denies any new symptoms at this time. However, she does report that she is still getting some chest pains sometimes and her breathing gets shallow. She notes that these episodes seem to last only a few minutes and then they disappear for a couple of weeks. When these episodes occur, she just takes the day nice and slow and does not push herself.

The patient reports that she has been trying to keep up with her medications regularly. She states that there are a lot of extra pills now, but she has a reminder app so she does pretty well. She denies any side effects from the medications at all except for the atenolol which makes her irritable in the beginning but now it doesn't seem to bother her as much.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.

• Head and Neck: No JVD detected.
• Respiratory: Reduced breath sounds bilaterally auscultation and percussion are clear. Breath normally.
• Cardiovascular: Regularly irregular rhythm with atrial fibrillation.
• Musculoskeletal: Trace peripheral edema on extremities.

We discussed lifestyle modifications including regular exercise as well as dietary changes to help manage symptoms.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that he has had the ulcer for approximately 2 months and it has recently become red and is draining. He denies any trauma to his foot, but believes he may have gotten it from walking barefoot on the beach. The patient did see his primary care physician (PCP) before coming in, who prescribed him medication for the ulcer. However, he has not yet filled the prescription.

The patient reports that his pain is intermittent and throbbing, but he does not have specific pain. He notes that he has not had this before.

The patient's diabetes is likely a major cause of this non-healing ulcer. He takes his diabetes medication, but does not check his blood sugar regularly. His last A1C was approximately 10, which is high.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Skin: Reports redness and drainage from the ulcer.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports throbbing pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: Vital signs are within normal limits. No fever present.
Skin Examination: There is a 1 x 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, proximal to the 5th MTP joint. There is some redness and drainage present. There is edema around it. Fluid is present coming out of it. No necrosis or odor present. No bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed in office today and there is no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Diabetic Foot Ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's diabetes likely contributed to this non-healing ulcer due to poor glycemic control.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with him how important it is to check his blood sugar regularly and follow up with his PCP for further treatment planning.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an ABI ankle brachial index to determine blood supply in his foot to see if we can heal that ulcer. I will also perform a debridement here today just to take off some dead tissue. I will prescribe clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for 7 days to try to get rid of that infection which he currently has and that will help reduce redness and drainage at this point in time.
- Additional Testing: ABI ankle brachial index will be ordered today.
- Surgical/Interventional Procedures: We will obtain a surgical shoe for him to wear while this is happening as wearing regular shoes can irritate it further and take him backwards in healing time.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of left ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 2 days ago when she slipped and fell on her left ankle. She was walking to her car when she slipped on ice and her left ankle twisted underneath her. She was able to get up afterwards but it was very sore and started swelling and quite a bit of pain, making it hard to walk.

The patient has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation which have provided some relief. She denies any pain above her ankle, including her calf or lower leg or knee.

The patient reports that she has been taking metformin for type 2 diabetes and that her blood sugars have been stable. She is also taking Norvasc for hypertension. Her last hemoglobin A1c was 6.8, which is good. She is due for an eye exam in the next couple of weeks.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left ankle pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea or vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without bruits.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally to auscultation.
Heart: Normal auscultation with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from previous exams.
Abdomen: Supple without masses or bruits.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the left ankle reveals tenderness over the lateral malleolus and tenderness over the 5th metatarsal bone. There is some swelling, redness, and pain with valgus stressing of the ankle.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the left ankle will be ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Left ankle sprain with possible fracture.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical examination findings are consistent with a left ankle sprain with possible fracture. The patient's symptoms began after she slipped on ice and fell on her left ankle, which would be consistent with an inversion injury leading to a sprain. However, there is also tenderness over the 5th metatarsal bone which could indicate a stress fracture.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today including wearing an air splint until we get the x-ray back as well as crutches until then. We also discussed avoiding weight bearing until we get the x-ray back to rule out a fracture. I encouraged her to continue exercising as well as continuing with metformin for diabetes management as well as continuing Norvasc for hypertension management.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an x-ray of the left ankle today in addition to prescribing Naprosyn 500 mg twice daily for pain control. We will also have her follow up in office once we receive the x-ray results if there is no fracture then we will have her take off the air splint and do partial weight bearing to see how it goes at that point in time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sore on the right foot.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Jenkins is a 43-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a right foot wound that has not healed. The patient reports that he initially did not feel that his new Hoka shoes were too tight, but a blister formed on his right foot. The blister soon became a wound and he was seen by his PCP, who placed him on a round of antibiotics, which he completed yesterday. He denies any changes to the appearance of the wound, denies pain or drainage, and occasionally has issues with stability, which was a primary purpose of purchasing these shoes. He denies any fever or chills. The patient reports neuropathy.

The patient has been wearing the same shoes for 2-3 weeks and has not had any trauma to his foot.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he used to see a podiatrist 2 years ago but they moved and he was unable to get another one.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is upset about having to change his shoes.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he completed antibiotics yesterday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports occasional issues with stability in his feet.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: Vital signs are stable at this time. Temperature is 98.1 degrees Fahrenheit, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respirations are 16 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 110/65 mmHg.
Neurological: Examination of bilateral lower extremities reveals no evidence of vascular compromise or gangrene. There are palpable bilateral femoral and popliteal pulses bilaterally but no palpable dorsalis pedis or plantar pulses bilaterally. Doppler signs are present bilaterally.
Skin: There is a 1 by 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the right fifth metatarsophalangeal joint with some yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no necrosis and there is no odor.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
In addition to reviewing the radiographic findings from prior visits today we also reviewed the x-ray images from prior visits which show no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Diabetic Foot Ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's last hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 8%. His current wound does not appear to be healing despite completion of antibiotics.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed how important it will be for him to get his diabetes under control in order for this wound to heal.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an ankle brachial index (ABI) today in order to determine if there is adequate blood supply to his foot for healing purposes. We will also perform debridement in office today in order to remove some dead tissue from the wound site. I have prescribed collagenase ointment for application once daily until we see improvement in wound size and coloration as well as healthy tissue formation at this point we will cover with dry sterile dressing daily until then we will continue this until we see improvement in wound size and coloration as well as healthy tissue formation at this point I have recommended that he wear a surgical shoe at all times due to lack of sensation in his feet which may cause further injury if left untreated at this point I do not think any more antibiotics are needed at this time.
- Additional Testing: We will schedule follow-up appointment in two weeks if there has been no improvement in wound size or coloration as well as healthy tissue formation at this point we may need to refer him to a vascular specialist if ABI indicates poor blood supply for healing purposes.

He notes that he is unable to play football due to his pain. The patient has tried NSAIDs in the past without relief and has attended physical therapy.

Musculoskeletal: Reports right hip, left calf, and big toe pain.

Hepatitis C.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Walker is a pleasant 68-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of her recent blood work results. The patient reports that she has been feeling fine, but is anxious about her recent blood work results, which revealed that she has hepatitis C. She denies ever being told in the past that she has hepatitis C. The patient reports that she used to party a lot and use IV drugs, but has been clean for over 15 years now. She also reports that she used to drink a lot more alcohol than she does now, and currently drinks approximately 1 beer per day, more on the weekends. The patient also reports that she used to smoke 1-2 packs per day, but has cut down to 1-2 cigarettes per day.

The patient states that she feels tired at the end of the day after working, but otherwise feels good. She denies any other medication conditions.

PAST HISTORY

Personal history of intravenous drug use over 15 years ago.
Family history significant for hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

None reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or jaundice.
Genitourinary: Denies urinary symptoms.
Skin: Denies rash or pruritus.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: In no apparent distress. No jaundice on skin exam.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with a grade 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated. This has not changed from last year and will continue to monitor as well.
Respiratory: Clear bilaterally with no wheezes, rales or rhonchi.
Gastrointestinal: Bowel sounds are present. Abdomen is soft with no hepatosplenomegaly appreciated on examination today.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

HCV antibody test was positive. Liver panel showed an elevated AST at 39 but ALT, albumin and total bilirubin were all within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Hepatitis C.
- Medical Reasoning: Initial labs are consistent with hepatitis C so based on our discussion today hepatitis C is a viral infection that affects the liver so you most likely have had it for years now. We discussed the next steps in confirming the diagnosis with additional blood work including checking HCV RNA as well as HCV genotype. We will also determine the severity of your liver disease by checking for fibrosis of the liver by ordering a special ultrasound with this information we will be able to know how to proceed as far as treatment.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today including antiviral medications and lifestyle modifications such as quitting smoking and reducing alcohol consumption if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will start by ordering additional blood work including HCV RNA testing as well as HCV genotype testing along with an ultrasound to assess for fibrosis of the liver at this point in time we will continue to monitor her closely for any changes in her liver function tests or symptoms.

Left shoulder pain.

The patient has been taking Advil and icing as much as possible for pain relief. This has provided him with some relief but not complete resolution of symptoms.

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mark Jackson is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began 3 weeks ago when he started playing tennis again. He notes that his pain is located on the outside of his elbow and is worse with activity and better with rest. He denies any trauma to the area. He has tried taking Tylenol and ibuprofen, but they do not provide relief. He also tried icing the area, but it did not help. The patient notes that he has been playing tennis more frequently than usual, which he attributes to his friend's encouragement to get off the couch and be more active.

The patient reports that his blood sugar levels have been elevated lately due to Easter candy consumption. His blood sugar levels have been in the 150s-160s.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of type 2 diabetes.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking metformin 500 mg twice a day, Flovent twice a day, and Albuterol as needed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies fever.
Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea or vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior exam.
MSK: Examination of the right elbow reveals moderate lateral epicondylar tenderness. Passive range of motion is painful with full extension but normal with flexion. Mild pain with resisted extension of the right wrist.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow today shows no acute fracture or other bony abnormality. No malalignment or joint effusion is present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute lateral epicondylitis (Tennis Elbow) Right Elbow.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with acute lateral epicondylitis (Tennis Elbow). This is likely due to overuse, as he has recently increased his tennis activity.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including rest, ice, bracing, and medication for pain control.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed a brace for his right forearm which will be provided by our nurse before discharge today. I have also prescribed Ultram 50 mg once per day for pain control which should help reduce discomfort in his right elbow.
- Additional Testing: We will follow up in 4 weeks to reevaluate his symptoms at that time if needed we will consider additional imaging or physical therapy referral depending on how he is doing at that time.
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood sugar levels are elevated lately due to Easter candy consumption and increased physical activity from playing tennis again.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed dietary modifications with him today including limiting carbohydrate intake and increasing fiber intake as well as increasing physical activity in moderation to help manage blood sugar levels better.
- Medical Treatment: I am going to increase his metformin dose to 1000 mg twice per day starting immediately today. I am also going to order a hemoglobin A1c level, CBC blood test, and chem-12 blood test today so we can check those results before making any further adjustments in treatment plan if needed at this point we will check his blood sugar twice daily for the next two weeks after which we can make additional adjustments if necessary at that point we will increase metformin dose again if necessary.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sandra Williams is a pleasant 68-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a kidney stone. She reports that she has had 7-8 kidney stones in the past and that she believes this is her 7th or 8th. She was seen in the emergency room last week, but she believes that she has passed this stone. She denies any blood in her urine at this time. She also denies any pain at this time.

The patient was treated with Percocet at the hospital for pain, which she believes helped her pass the stone. She has not seen a urologist in a while, but she did see someone approximately 1 year ago.

The patient reports that her blood pressure is usually well-controlled at home, but her blood pressure was elevated to 150/90 mmHg today. She denies any chest pain or abdominal pain today.

She also reports that she has been having difficulty controlling her diet due to being on-the-go and having trouble preparing healthy meals. She does not know if she can make changes on her own or if she needs help with diet counseling.

The patient also reports that she has a history of hypertension and diabetes. Her A1c was 6.7 when last seen, which is slightly elevated from when it was first diagnosed approximately 1 year ago. However, it has decreased slightly since then. The patient reports that her blood sugar levels have been good lately, although she does not check them often.

PAST HISTORY

History of hypertension.
History of diabetes.
History of kidney stones.
History of insomnia.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally without wheezes or rales.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Urine analysis and culture will be ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Kidney stones are present but I believe they have passed this time. We will obtain a urinalysis and urine culture to confirm everything is cleared up.
I will refer the patient to urology for further evaluation and management of recurrent kidney stones.
Hypertension is well controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily at home, but elevated to 150/90 mmHg today in office. We will continue with Norvasc as prescribed and monitor blood pressure at home more frequently.
Type 2 diabetes is well controlled on Metformin 500 mg daily at home, but elevated A1c was last seen at 6.7 when initially diagnosed approximately 1 year ago. However, it has decreased slightly since then. The patient reports that her blood sugar levels have been good lately, although she does not check them often.
I recommend that the patient start checking her blood sugar levels before each meal to gauge where she is and adjust accordingly so we can determine how much food she should be eating based on those readings.
Insomnia: The patient reports that sometimes stays awake due to worrying about things; however, using meditation apps helps with sleep quality. I advised the patient to try practicing proper sleep hygiene by turning off electronics before bedtime, keeping the room dark and cool, and avoiding caffeine close to bedtime as these are all effective strategies for improving sleep quality without medication.
The patient denied using melatonin previously but did try it once without improvement; however, I am willing to prescribe melatonin as needed for sleep support if needed in the future.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right upper lobe lung nodule.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Rodriguez is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a right upper lobe lung nodule. The patient reports that he has had a cough for approximately 3 months, which began when he was loading horses. He denies any previous history of lung infections or pneumonia. The patient is a former smoker, having stopped smoking approximately 7 years ago. He reports that his rheumatoid arthritis is well-controlled with methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly and that he exercises regularly, including biking.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he has a history of rheumatoid arthritis.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that his mother had breast cancer but is doing well.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he takes methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies fever.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Respiratory: Denies productive cough, hemoptysis, or dyspnea on exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi present.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs. No extra heartbeats appreciated.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of chest demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. The nodule appears smooth in appearance and no evidence of emphysematous disease is present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Kyle Rodriguez is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a right upper lobe lung nodule.
1. Right upper lobe lung nodule.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's CT scan demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe which appears smooth in appearance and no evidence of emphysematous disease is present. Given his smoking history, I believe it would be best to have this removed via video-assisted thoracoscopy.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks and benefits of surgery as well as alternative options such as observation with serial CT scans. I encouraged him to ask questions and express any concerns he may have regarding his treatment plan.
- Medical Treatment: We will order pulmonary function tests (PFT) to obtain a baseline for his lung function. A PET CT will be ordered to determine if this nodule is metabolically active (i.e., lights up). We will proceed with video-assisted thoracoscopy to remove this nodule along with a small portion of his lung under general anesthesia. He will be admitted overnight post-procedure and have a chest tube placed until it can be removed at bedside on the next day.
2. Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current medication regimen appears adequate for controlling his symptoms at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continued follow-up with his rheumatologist and adherence to his current medication regimen.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

Kyle Rodriguez is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a right upper lobe lung nodule.
1. Right upper lobe lung nodule.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks and benefits of surgery as well as alternative options such as observation with serial CT scans. I encouraged him to ask questions and express any concerns he may have regarding his treatment plan.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continued follow-up with his rheumatologist and adherence to his current medication regimen.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and instability.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain and instability. The onset of his symptoms began when he was playing basketball with his son, Sean. He was attempting a shot when he landed awkwardly and rolled and twisted his right ankle. He reports that he can no longer walk on it due to pain and instability. He has been having trouble walking, but he can stand on it. He denies any numbness or tingling in his right foot or ankle.

The patient reports that he recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine, which he had been doing prior to the onset of his symptoms. He denies any previous history of similar injuries.

PAST HISTORY

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and instability.
Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient works from home and plans to coach his son’s basketball team in 04/2022.
Patient enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals swelling on the lateral side of the ankle. There is exquisite tenderness over the lateral aspect of the ankle with palpation. There is mild tenderness over the medial deltoid region as well. Brisk capillary refill is present bilaterally without any signs of edema or erythema. No malalignment is present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays were obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right lateral malleolar fracture.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with right ankle pain and instability, which began after an injury while playing basketball with his son. His x-ray revealed a displaced lateral malleolus at Weber C level, which is consistent with this diagnosis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for this injury today, including surgery, which will require 3 months of recovery time. We also discussed alternative options for coaching his son’s basketball team during this time period.
- Medical Treatment: We will start him on meloxicam for pain management today. I have also prescribed ice packs to reduce swelling as well as elevation to reduce swelling further at home. I have also recommended that he use crutches for ambulation until we see improvement in his symptoms.
- Additional Testing: X-rays were obtained today, not yet reviewed.

Facial pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 54-year-old male who presents for the evaluation of facial pain. He reports right-sided facial pain. He denies left-sided facial pain. He reports headaches. He denies sensory loss, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek. He denies right-sided facial weakness. Teeth are symmetric.

The onset of his symptoms began 2-3 months ago and have been gradually worsening over time. The patient describes his pain as stabbing and shooting in nature, particularly in the right cheek bone area. The pain is sometimes accompanied by a sensation of heat and can be triggered by certain temperatures or cold temperatures. The patient has tried ibuprofen and Motrin without relief, as well as applying Tiger Balm to the area without success.

The patient has had episodes of pain that last from a few minutes to up to an hour in duration. He denies any history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss, fevers, chills.
• Neurological: Reports right-sided facial pain; Denies left-sided facial pain; Reports headaches; Denies sensory loss, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek; Denies right-sided facial weakness.

Neurological Examination: Cranial nerves II-XII are intact bilaterally with no signs of weakness or deficits.

RESULTS

- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 44-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began when she was skiing in Vermont last weekend. She was coming off the lift when she caught her ski and fell, and her knee popped. She has been unable to bear weight on her right knee since the injury. She reports that she is unable to bend or straighten her right knee, but it does somewhat straighten with pain.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in her toes. She is a very active person who enjoys skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit, so it is just the patient and the children at home. The patient reports that she has been using crutches since the injury.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Reports she is otherwise healthy and denies a history of high blood pressure or diabetes.
Social: Very active with skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit.
MEDICATIONS

Ibuprofen.
ALLERGIES

No known allergies.
note.objective_exam:

CV: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neck: Supple without masses or lymphadenopathy.
Gastrointestinal: No abdominal masses or tenderness.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals edema and effusion over the right knee. There is pain to palpation over the right lateral knee joint. Decreased flexion and extension are present. A positive Lachman sign is present bilaterally, however, only on the left side today due to bilateral swelling in both knees at this time. Palpable dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are present bilaterally.

RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right Knee Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury while skiing in Vermont last weekend when she caught her ski on a lift bar while coming off it, causing her right knee to pop out of place. This resulted in significant pain, swelling, and decreased range of motion in her right knee. We have reviewed X-rays from today which did not show any bony abnormalities but we are concerned that she may have ruptured her ACL (anterior cruciate ligament). We have ordered an MRI for further evaluation as well as an arthrogram for better visualization of any potential ligamentous injuries.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continuing ibuprofen as needed for pain control, wearing a brace for support, and follow-up with us once we receive our MRI results for further evaluation and treatment planning.
- Medical Treatment Plan: Continue ibuprofen 600-800 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain control. Wear a brace for support at home.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Beverly Ortiz is a 24-year-old female who presents for her yearly exam. She has a history of type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. She has been working at a bakery this summer, which has been super fun. She has really been enjoying working there, but she finds herself snacking a lot during shifts and eating a lot more desserts than she normally would.

Her blood sugars have been up and down because of her diet, she thinks, because she has not missed any of her medication. Her diet has been pretty bad lately.

Her blood pressure is good despite her diabetes levels being up and down. She is sleeping well and denies any concerns about hurting herself or anything like that.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Reports increased appetite for sweets.
Genitourinary: Denies urinary frequency or urgency.
Skin: Denies rash or pruritus.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination:
- General Appearance: Well-nourished in appearance today in no acute distress.
- Skin: No edema, no erythema, no lesions, no scars.
- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left sternal border. No gallops, rales, or rubs. No murmurs other than the grade 2 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border.
- Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally in all lung fields. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi present.
- Neurological: Intact to light touch throughout all extremities. Normal sensation to light touch throughout all extremities. Normal grip strength bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c is elevated as well as blood sugars have been elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1) Diabetes Mellitus Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood sugars have been elevated due to her diet. She is still taking metformin twice daily as prescribed but reports that her diet has been pretty bad lately due to her new job at the bakery which she enjoys but finds it challenging to resist the temptation of the desserts there.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I counseled her on the importance of dietary changes to help control her blood sugar levels. I advised her to cut down on snacking and additional sweets and check her blood sugar in the morning for 2 weeks so we can know what her first fasting blood sugar was in the morning then we will come back and see her in about 2 months to see if everything has straightened out if not then we will talk about adding another medication.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin twice daily as prescribed without change at this point due to dietary related issues only at this time.
2) Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood pressure is good despite diabetes levels being up and down. She is sleeping well and denies any concerns about hurting herself or anything like that.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I counseled her on the importance of continuing with current medication regimen without any changes at this point as it seems to be doing well currently.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily without change at this point.

Back pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Rebecca Thompson is a 27-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began 1 month ago when she started swimming more regularly. She has been swimming freestyle with her legs kicking straight out, but she has noticed that her symptoms started after 2 laps. She was able to swim 10 laps without any pain initially, but after a couple of laps, it starts to hurt. She denies any history of injury.

The patient reports that she has been doing well with her chronic back pain, which comes and goes. She denies any lower extremity pain or weakness. The patient reports that she has been doing well with her depression and medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Psychological: Denies suicidal ideation or intent.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without tenderness to palpation. No adenopathy present.
Respiratory: Clear bilaterally to auscultation.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs or gallops.
Gastrointestinal: Normal bowel sounds present.
Musculoskeletal:
- Examination of the right knee: Swelling is absent in the joint space. Pain is present with range of motion of the knee, particularly with patellar inhibition. Grip strength is equal bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was reviewed in office today and shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation. The x-ray is otherwise unremarkable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Chondromalacia of the patella.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with chondromalacia of the patella due to overuse from swimming.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for this condition today, including anti-inflammatories and physical therapy exercises for strengthening her quadriceps muscle. We also discussed avoiding activities that put extra pressure on her knees for a little while until it gets better.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribe ibuprofen 600 mg four times a day with food as needed for anti-inflammatory effects. Prescribe straight leg raising exercises to strengthen quadriceps muscle.
- Additional Testing: X-ray was reviewed in office today and shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation.
2. Chronic back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms have been well controlled at this point in time but we will continue to monitor her progress at home and contact us if it flares up again.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for this condition today, including continuing swimming as long as it does not flare up again at home.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current medication as prescribed by another provider at this time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who presents for a return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was last seen in August 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome that was treated with Bentyl.

The patient reports that she has been going out to eat on Friday nights and Saturdays and has had some spicy foods or spicy shrimp. She denies that her gut likes it at all. The patient states that she is starting to notice that she is having a bowel movement between 2-3 times per day on normal days. Her stools are described as formed. She also reports that after drinking alcohol with friends, she tends to have more diarrhea.

The patient notes that she usually eats pasta at Fridays restaurant and the chicken alfredo. She states that it normally does not bother her but notes that pasta can make her bloated. Grilled chicken is usually okay but the alfredo sauce is higher in fat and contains dairy. The patient prefers Patron but will drink brown liquor only if she gets two drinks. Occasionally, she will drink a martini.

She denies any luck using the fiber like Citrucel regularly.

The patient reports that during the week, she eats like usual but has been avoiding heavy foods due to cramping and sharp pains. She did have some fried chicken today though and everything was alright after that.

She understands the importance of portion sizes and can't go without fried chicken at least once in a while.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of poor eating habits and poor sleeping habits as well as high stress.

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with IBS with functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.

• Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged dietary modifications such as avoiding greasy or fatty foods, sugary drinks, alcohol consumption as well as starting a neuromodulator such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS.
• Medical Treatment: Prescribed Citrucel tablet twice daily for regularity. Prescribed Bentyl 20 mg as needed 30-45 minutes prior to eating out at a restaurant. Prescribed Zofran if needed but advised to reduce triggers before taking Zofran. Prescribed Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for long-term management of IBS symptoms.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands the importance of portion sizes and agrees to follow up in one month via MyChart regarding any side effects or issues or if adjustments are needed.

Adult hydrocephalus.

Mr. Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

The patient was status post shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020, with a Medtronic Strata programmable shunt in the ventricular peritoneal configuration placed at a level of 2.0. He was status post CT scan of the head from 10/15/2020, which revealed frontal horn span at the level of foramen of Munro of 4.6 cm, 3rd ventricular contour flat with span of 10 mm, substantial small vessel ischemic change.

The patient reports that he has been doing much better since his shunt surgery. His walking has improved and he is now able to walk to the dining room just fine. However, he still has times where he needs assistance. His bladder control did improve after surgery but has leveled out and he is now wearing diapers. He denies any issues with sores from wearing the diaper or decreased or painful urination.

He also reports that his cognitive impairment has improved and he feels like he can have a normal conversation with someone again.

The patient denies any headaches or pain where the shunt is and denies any pain in his belly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers or unintentional weight loss.
• Genitourinary: Reports urinary incontinence and wearing a diaper.
• Neurological: Reports continued walking impairment and cognitive impairment.
• Psychiatric: Denies depression, excessive worrying, or mood swings.

Sexual health concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Ross is a 23-year-old female who presents for a full spectrum STD testing. She reports symptoms of discomfort, a change in discharge, and odor in her vaginal region. She denies any fevers or chills. The patient states that she recently learned that her partner has been in sexual encounters with other people for quite some time. She wants to be evaluated for all STDs.

The patient reports that she started noticing some weird discharge last week. The discharge smells different and is not the same color or consistency as usual. This did not phase her until she noticed that the right side of her vagina was hurting, which has not gone away.

The patient has been with her boyfriend for 3 years. She believes he started cheating on her approximately 3 months ago.

PAST HISTORY

Abnormal Pap Smear around the age of 20; Normal Pap Smears since then, including the most recent one approximately 6 months ago.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: Normal vital signs.
• Pelvic Examination: Demonstrates no external lesions. Normal labia majora and labia minora. Normal physiological discharge, with normal color and smell.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

STD Testing: Gonorrhea, Chlamydia, Trichomoniasis were done today in office and sent out for laboratory analysis.
Blood work for Syphilis, HIV, and Hepatitis C was also done today in office.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Is screen for STD.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with symptoms of vaginal discomfort, change in discharge, and odor in her vaginal region. She denies any fevers or chills. • Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks associated with having multiple sexual partners and the importance of regular Pap smears to screen for cervical cancer.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed the results of her STD testing today and will call if anything is abnormal. If she has not heard from us by 3 days from today we can call back at that point to discuss results further.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Tyler Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. Last time he was seen, he received a steroid injection in his right knee. He reports that the injection did not help, and his symptoms have returned. He states that his right knee is still swollen, and he is experiencing pain. The pain level is approximately 3 out of 10 at the moment, but it typically increases to 6 on a normal day. He has been swollen for approximately 2 months now.

The patient reports that he has tried wearing compression socks to help with swelling, but they have not been helpful. He also notes that he has slowed down a bit and found it difficult to do things quickly due to his pain. When he sits for a while, the pain becomes worse, and he experiences stiffness when getting up from a seated position. He uses a cane to get his bearings and notes that after a little while, the stiffness loosens up.

The patient reports that he has been taking Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily and Celebrex 200 mg daily as prescribed by his primary care physician. He notes that the Celebrex has helped with pain until the swelling started again.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he received a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021.

MEDICATIONS

Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily.
Celebrex 200 mg daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right lower extremity reveals mild edema over the distal portion of the leg bilaterally. Range of motion slightly diminished in all directions with pain upon full extension of the right knee joint. Capillary refill is normal in both feet.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Fluid aspiration and steroid injection procedure performed today.
Risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained to the patient today including hypopigmentation, soft tissue atrophy, tendon ruptures, and transient hypoglycemia among others.
Verbal consent was obtained from Mr. Nelson prior to proceeding with the procedure today.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right knee effusion with inflammation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis with right knee effusion and inflammation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative treatments including dietary modifications such as reducing salt intake as well as elevating his legs at night when possible.
- Medical Treatment: We will proceed with an x-ray of both knees today to evaluate for any bony abnormalities contributing to his current symptoms.
- Additional Testing: We will also schedule physical therapy for both knees today as well as obtain x-rays of both knees today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents for a follow-up examination. She was previously seen for perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. She reports that she has been using doxycycline cream and MetroCream. She started using doxycycline cream twice a day but noticed improvement and then changed to once a day. She reports that the rash has plateaued and is not improving. She stopped breastfeeding and started taking doxycycline at that time.

The patient denies any other medications or supplements.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Reports perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Fitzpatrick skin type IV.
Bilateral medial cheeks: There are a few faint erythematous papules and just maybe a little bit of redness around and underneath the nostrils.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms have plateaued with the current treatment plan of doxycycline cream once daily. We discussed alternative treatments such as Elidel cream which is not covered by insurance but may be more cost-effective than Eucrisa ointment.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks associated with oral doxycycline as well as the benefits of topical treatments such as Elidel cream or Eucrisa ointment. The patient understands that she can resume taking doxycycline twice daily if needed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue using MetroCream twice daily until rash resolves. Increase use of doxycycline to twice daily until rash resolves. Apply tacrolimus ointment to affected area twice daily until rash resolves. After rash resolves, discontinue tacrolimus ointment for 1 week before resuming MetroCream once daily for an additional week before stopping.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right upper quadrant pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago. He describes the pain as severe and squeezing in nature, which is located on the right side of his abdomen, just below his ribs. The pain comes and goes but when it does, it is very severe and he becomes nauseated and sick to his stomach. He rates his pain an 8 out of 10.

The patient reports that his pain is related to eating. He states that most of the time his pain occurs immediately after he eats, but it can also occur 2-3 hours after he eats. He notes that he has been trying to cut back on fatty foods since he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, but he still experiences pain.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with weight loss since he started a keto diet. He has lost 25 pounds over the last 3 months and his blood sugar levels have improved. However, he still experiences right upper quadrant pain.

The patient reports that both of his parents have had cholecystectomies due to cholelithiasis.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise.
Social History: Enjoys nature photography.
Family History: Family history of cholelithiasis. Both parents have had cholecystectomies.
MEDICATIONS

Currently managing type 2 diabetes with diet and exercise.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Oxygen saturation on room air is 99%. No wheezes or rales are heard bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's abdominal ultrasound shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. His symptoms have not improved with dietary modifications alone, so we will proceed with surgical intervention.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks and benefits of surgery today in detail, including post-operative care and follow-up appointments.
• Medical Treatment: We will proceed with a laparoscopic cholecystectomy today.
• Additional Testing: None required at this time.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Musculoskeletal: Reports left-sided upper extremity pain.

PAST HISTORY

History of a right total knee arthroplasty 2 years ago, in spring of 2020. He states that his right knee feels 95% improved since the surgery.

MEDICATIONS

Tylenol; Ibuprofen.
