Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her symptoms began 4 days ago. She reports that she has been doing some pottery and has been working on a ceramic bowl. She denies any history of trauma to the elbow. The patient reports that her pain is located on the medial aspect of her right elbow and radiates down her arm. She rates her pain at 7/10 at its worst. The patient reports that she has not been able to work on her pottery due to the pain.

The patient denies any history of injury to the elbow.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2.

MEDICATIONS

The patient is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
Genitourinary: Denies dysuria, hematuria, or urinary incontinence.
Skin: Denies rash or lesions.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck and Neck Structures: Supple neck with no evidence of cervical spine tenderness or mass effect.
Respiratory: Auscultation of Lungs reveals clear bilaterally to bilaterally to auscultation. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi are heard. No gallop rhythm is present. No murmurs are heard at the left sternal border or over the right second intercostal space. No rubs are present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow reveals no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right Elbow Pain (Medial Epicondylitis)
- Medical Reasoning: The x-ray examination was unremarkable for any bony abnormalities, which supports our diagnosis of medial epicondylitis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient that we will need to hold off on pottery for a couple weeks in order for her arm to heal properly.
- Medical Treatment: We have ordered a sling for her right arm which she can wear while awake. We have also prescribed ice for 20 minutes, 3 times per day as well as ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food for one week. We will follow up in two weeks if there is no improvement in symptoms.
2. Diabetes Type 2 Management Plan Change - Increase Metformin Dose from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily and Initiate A1c Testing in Two Weeks if Blood Sugar Levels do not improve with increased medication dose.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood sugar levels have been elevated at times when she has not taken her medication as prescribed, which may be contributing to her elevated blood sugar levels at times when she does take it as prescribed.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient that we will need to increase her metformin dose from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily as well as initiate A1c testing in two weeks if blood sugar levels do not improve with increased medication dose.
3. Hypertension Management Plan Change - Continue Lisinopril at current dose of 10 mg once daily.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood pressure has been stable on lisinopril at this dose, which suggests that this medication is effective in controlling her hypertension at this dose.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient that we will continue lisinopril at current dose of 10 mg once daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that she has had this ulcer for approximately 1 year. She denies any trauma to the foot, but states that she developed a blister and then picked at it, which became red and infected. She was treated with antibiotics, which seemed to improve her symptoms initially, but they have not resolved. The patient reports that she has been experiencing increased drainage from the wound and is feeling more tired lately. She denies any pain in her foot, but reports decreased sensation in her foot.

The patient's medical history includes type 2 diabetes and neuropathy. Her last hemoglobin A1c was 10, and she is currently taking insulin and metformin. She has been on antibiotic treatment with Keflex for 5 months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Neurological: Reports decreased sensation in her right foot.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in her right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: Vital signs are stable at this time.
Neurological Examination: Examination of the right lower extremity reveals decreased sensation over the lateral aspect of the foot distal to L5. No motor strength testing was performed due to decreased sensation.
Skin Examination: There is a 1 x 2 cm circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the 5th MTP joint. There is yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. No surrounding erythema or cellulitis is present. There is no evidence of fluid collection or necrosis around the wound site. No odor is appreciated, and there is no bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed prior to today's visit and revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with diabetic neuropathy and non-healing diabetic foot ulcer.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for her current symptoms today, including debridement, colaganase ointment application, surgical shoe prescription, and follow-up appointment in two weeks.
• Medical Treatment: Debridement will be performed in office today. Colaganase ointment will be prescribed for application once daily until further improvement is seen. Surgical shoes will be prescribed for wear at all times until further improvement or resolution of symptoms.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up after STEMI.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Anderson is a 74-year-old female who presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where we had to put in another stent. She was doing well after her last heart attack, but she started having this horrible chest pain that wouldn’t go away. She went to the emergency room and was told she needed another stent. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath since her last visit. She has been walking her dog every day for the past 6 months, which is approximately 1.5 to 2 miles per day. She is looking forward to seeing family and having nice weather during the holidays.

She has noticed that her legs are a little swollen since she was sent home from the hospital.

She has been taking her medications as prescribed and affords them with good insurance.

She has not adjusted her diet since her last heart attack, but she will have to go back to watching her salt intake. She loves pizza and tries (a type of food).

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and diabetes.
Patient reports history of RCA stent placement in 2018.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports walking her dog daily and enjoys pizza and tries (a type of food).

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking aspirin 81 mg daily; Brilinta 90 mg twice daily; Lipitor 80 mg daily; Toprol 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention. No carotid bruits.
Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
Respiratory: Clear bilaterally over auscultation.
Extremities: Lower extremity edema, pitting grade +1 on right radial artery. Right radial artery pulses are palpable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
EKG: Normal sinus rhythm, good R wave progression, evolutionary changes anticipated after STEMI.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Coronary Artery Disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where we had to put in another stent. Her symptoms have resolved with medical treatment but she is now experiencing new symptoms consistent with another STEMI. We are going to continue to evaluate this over time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of adhering to medication regimen and making dietary changes in order to improve cardiac health.
- Medical Treatment: Continue aspirin 81 mg daily and Brilinta 90 mg twice daily. Continue on high dose statin Lipitor at 80 mg/day. Continue on Toprol at 50 mg/day. Refer patient to cardiac rehab for education and exercise therapy.
2. Reduced Left Ventricular Dysfunction with Moderate Mitral Regurgitation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s ECHO revealed reduced ejection fraction of 35%. This is concerning given her history of STEMI but it should improve over time given that she is compliant with medication regimen.
The patient was placed in the cath lab quickly so it appears that there was some muscle damage but it should recover given that she is compliant with medication regimen.
The patient also has moderate mitral regurgitation which may be contributing factor to reduced ejection fraction however this should also improve over time given that she is compliant with medication regimen.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of adhering to medication regimen in order to improve cardiac health.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril at 20 mg/day due to fluid retention however add aldactone at.125 mg/day due to hypertension concerns. Repeat ECHO in approximately two months.

The patient reports that since his heart attack 6 months ago, he has been experiencing dizziness when standing up quickly. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that his hemoglobin A1c was 16, but his glucose is approximately 130 fasting. He notes that he has not been watching his sweets well and admits to having an affinity for chocolate chip cookies.

The patient reports that his last time seeing a nephrologist was approximately 1 year ago. He denies any kidney problems.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Heart attack, coronary artery disease, diabetes.
Surgical: Stent placement at the left anterior descending artery.
SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with his dog. San Francisco 49ers fan.
note.objective_exam:

- Medical Treatment: Continue aspirin, Brilinta, fish oil, Crestor 40 mg once daily as prescribed. Refill medications automatically through the computer system at the patient’s preferred pharmacy.
- Additional Testing: No further testing is needed at this time but we will follow up if symptoms develop again.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of following up with his nephrologist regularly to monitor kidney function and adjust treatment accordingly.
- Medical Treatment: Refer to Dr. Miller for appointment to follow up with nephrologist in office for regular monitoring of kidney function and adjustment of treatment plan as needed.

We discussed dietary education with the dietitian to help him improve blood glucose control further and we will also discuss insulin regimen with primary care physician in office today.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Outpatient EMG/NCV ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Right carpal tunnel syndrome.

George Young is a 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago when he was playing lacrosse with his children. He describes the pain as sharp and radiates down his forearm. He denies any history of trauma to the area. He has tried taking Advil, which he believes has helped somewhat.

The patient reports that he is active in playing lacrosse with his children and notes that he is getting too old for this activity.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Hypertension, Diabetes.
Social History: Plays lacrosse with his children.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 20 mg daily; Metformin 500 mg daily.
Allergies: None listed.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck and Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. No chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left sternal border. No gallops, rubs, or murmurs at the auscultation of the apex.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow was obtained today and reviewed in office today. There is no evidence of a fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right elbow contusion.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to his right elbow when he was hit by a lacrosse stick while playing with his son. This resulted in swelling and inflammation in the olecranon area of the posterior elbow as well as bruising at this site.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for this injury today including rest, ice, compression, elevation (RICE) as well as over-the-counter ibuprofen for pain management.
- Medical Treatment: Prescription for 800 mg ibuprofen twice daily for pain management and ice 3 times a day for 20 minutes at a time to help reduce swelling and pain. We advised him not to play lacrosse with his son for the next couple of weeks to allow time for healing before returning to play.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure was elevated at 150/90 mmHg today but we believe this may be white coat hypertension given that he denies any symptoms associated with hypertension such as headaches or dizziness.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including dietary changes such as reducing salt intake which he has been doing since the pandemic when he fell off track with eating more than usual but has been compliant since then.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily as prescribed.
3. Diabetes Mellitus Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood glucose levels have been stable between 80-100 mg/dL without insulin therapy which is good given that he does not check his blood glucose regularly due to not taking insulin yet.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including dietary changes such as reducing salt intake which he has been doing since the pandemic when he fell off track with eating more than usual but has been compliant since then. We also discussed regular follow-up appointments to monitor blood glucose levels and adjust medication if necessary if needed in the future.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin 500 mg daily as prescribed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated cholesterol.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary patient who presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. The patient is an imminesipated minor. She reports that she was recently screened for cholesterol at her annual checkup and her results were elevated. She was advised to follow up with me. The patient denies any history of hypercholesterolemia or other lipid disorders at an early age. She does have a family history of heart disease, as her cousin died of a heart attack in his 40s. The patient enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails, but she admits to consuming chocolate chip cookies regularly. She tries to eat a clean diet most days, but she is surprised that her cholesterol was high given her healthy eating habits.

The patient has been active in the past, but she has not been as active lately due to the warm weather. She has been biking with friends and enjoying the outdoors.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports no significant past medical history.
Family history: Cousin died of a heart attack in their 40s.
Social history: Parents smoked when they lived with them.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports no medications.
Allergies: None reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies fatigue or weight loss.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or nausea or vomiting.
Psychiatric: Denies depression or anxiety.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs appreciated in all cardiac auscultations.
LUNGS: Clear bilaterally to auscultation and percussion.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cholesterol level was elevated at 210.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Elevated cholesterol.
- Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all children be screened for cholesterol once they become between ages 9 and 11 and again between ages 17 and 20. Studies have shown a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks. We will order a full cholesterol panel, glucose, complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, liver panels, and genetic testing to see if this problem is familial or secondary in nature.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of dietary changes including limiting saturated fats and sugars. I encouraged the patient to meet with a nutritionist for further guidance on healthy eating habits. We also discussed the importance of continued exercise such as biking which she enjoys doing regularly.
- Medical Treatment: We will follow up in 3-6 months after implementing dietary changes with another cholesterol level check.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of chest pain. She reports that she has been experiencing chest pain for approximately 3 months. The onset of her chest pain is typically when she starts walking, and it is described as a dull pressure. She denies radiating the pain to her back or arms. The patient denies shortness of breath, sweats, or clamminess at the onset of her chest pain. She notes that the chest pain resolves once she stops walking.

The patient reports that she has been trying to increase her activity level but has not been able to keep up with her usual activities due to the chest pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she has a history of diabetes type 2 and high blood pressure.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that she has a family history of heart disease.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is currently taking metformin 500 mg twice daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss, fever, chills, or night sweats.
• Cardiovascular: Denies dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or palpitations.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies muscle weakness or joint pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No JVD. No carotid bruits.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• EKG was reviewed in office today and shows no signs of a heart attack.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Chest Pain: Initial evaluation revealed stable angina. The patient will be referred to cardiology for further evaluation and stress testing. We discussed the plan in detail with the patient today and she understands what we are going to do. We also discussed aspirin therapy and nitroglycerin therapy in case of worsening symptoms.
• Diabetes Type 2: The patient is doing fairly well on metformin 500 mg twice daily. We discussed dietary changes with her today and encouraged her to continue exercising regularly. We also discussed an eye exam for diabetic retinopathy at ophthalmology today. I have ordered another hemoglobin A1c today which will be reviewed in 2 weeks if necessary.
• Hypertension: Trending high blood pressure on multiple clinic visits over the past few years. I have started the patient on hydrochlorothiazide at home and have instructed her to monitor her blood pressure daily in the morning when she wakes up using an ambulatory blood pressure monitor at home and enter her findings into Epic MyChart daily until we see each other again in 2 weeks.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago. She denies any specific event that caused the pain. The patient describes her pain as a deep achy pain located behind her patella, which she feels like she can hear creaking in her knees. She notes that her pain is worse with ambulation from a seated position, stair climbing, and watching TV. Her pain improves with rest.

The patient reports that she has tried ice and an ACE bandage in the past. She also takes ibuprofen or Aleve occasionally but tries to avoid taking any medications due to side effects. She has been running 5-6 miles per day but has had to decrease her mileage significantly due to knee pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she sustained an upper extremity fracture in 6th grade.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking ibuprofen and Aleve.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports bilateral knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple, no masses or lymphadenopathy.
Respiratory: Auscultation of Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Auscultation of Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs.
Musculoskeletal Examination:
Gait: Normal gait pattern bilaterally.
Abduction Strength: 3/5 bilaterally.
Lower Extremity Strength: 5/5 bilaterally.
Knee Examination:
- Palpation of bilateral retinacula reveals tenderness to palpation bilaterally.
- Patellar grind test is positive bilaterally.
- Squatting causes bilateral knee pain, but Lachman anterior and posterior drawer and McMurray tests are negative bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed in office today. There are no fractures or osteoarthritis present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Bilateral patellofemoral pain syndrome was diagnosed based on the patient's history, physical examination, and radiographic findings today. The patient's symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis, which is a common condition that causes knee pain in active young individuals. This condition is related to the way the patella moves along the femoral groove. Treatment options include medication for symptom management and physical therapy to increase lower extremity strength, mobility, and correct any incorrect running mechanics that may be contributing to her symptoms.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diane Baker is a 28-year-old female with a past medical history significant for depression and hypertension who presents for emergency room follow-up. She reports that her blood pressure was elevated in the emergency room yesterday. She states that she went for a walk because it was sunny and she felt light-headed, and she started to fall. Her boyfriend caught her, and they went right to the emergency room. Her blood pressure was elevated to almost 200 mmHg at that time. She denies any headache at that time, but does report that she had a headache today.

She has been experiencing high blood pressure once a week or less often, which usually resolves once she is back on her regular diet and routine after traveling for work. She states that she does not bring her blood pressure cuff with her when traveling.

She is compliant with taking lisinopril as prescribed.

The patient reports that she has been doing well with therapy for depression, which she started last year. She has been attending therapy once per week and finds it helpful. Her support system includes her boyfriend, mom, and brother, who are all very close to her.

The patient denies any chest pain or shortness of breath at this time. She does report some nasal congestion due to seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Respiratory: Reports nasal congestion due to seasonal allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neurological: No carotid bruits in the neck.
• Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the heart in all views.
• Respiratory: Clear lungs bilaterally. Trace pitting edema to the lower extremities bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Electrocardiogram stable in comparison to last year shows no new changes from chronic high blood pressure.
Echocardiogram from just a few months ago shows slightly leaky heart valve with no treatment options available at this time. The heart murmur is stable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. High Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure was elevated in the emergency room yesterday, but has been stable since then. She reports that her blood pressure usually resolves once she is back on her regular diet and routine after traveling for work.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications such as increasing physical activity, reducing sodium intake, and avoiding caffeine and alcohol in moderation as well as dietary changes when traveling for work.
The patient will continue to check her blood pressures at home daily and report them to me through the patient portal. We will make adjustments as necessary if needed at this point we will also consider adding a second agent if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: Lisinopril increased to 40 mg once daily if necessary we may need to add a second agent if necessary.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that therapy has been helpful for managing symptoms of depression at this point we do not feel it is necessary to start medication but you can contact me if you need anything in the future.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative management options such as therapy which has been helpful for you so far but you can contact me if you need anything in the future.
The patient will continue attending therapy once per week.

Neck

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluating a 60-year-old right-handed male for the evaluation of numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient presents today for the evaluation of numbness and tingling in both hands. He reports that he has been experiencing this for a few weeks. The onset of his symptoms began after he broke his wrists in a motor vehicle accident in December 2019. He was treated with a splint, which has provided some relief. However, his symptoms have worsened over the last month. He also reports mild stiffness in his neck, which he sustained from the accident as well.

The patient describes the location of his symptoms as being on this side from here to here up to about here, and on the other side from here to here. He notes that he experiences pain, soreness, and weakness in his hands, especially when using them. The pain is more pronounced at night and comes and goes throughout the day. The patient denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers, but notes that they may be less sensitive than they should be.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension (taking Coreg) and anxiety (taking Lexapro). He also reports a history of prediabetes (controlled via dietary changes). Additionally, he reports a history of motor vehicle accident in December 2019 resulting in broken wrists; history of neck contusion from the accident; history of gout and muscle pain; history of floaters in eyes; history of dry, itchy skin and nail bed changes; history of easily fatigued and weight gain; history of excessive hunger and abdominal bloating; history of bilateral peripheral edema and shortness of breath.

MEDICATIONS

The patient is currently taking Coreg for hypertension and Lexapro for anxiety.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
Gastrointestinal: Reports excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Reports floaters.
Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Reports always hungry.
Skin: Reports nail bed changes, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Reports gout and muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurological Examination:
Right hand examination reveals decreased sensation to pinprick over third and fourth fingers bilaterally. Reflexes are 1+ bilaterally symmetric at knees with downgoing toes bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
EMG testing was performed today due to bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially cubital tunnel syndrome.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially cubital tunnel syndrome.
1. Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptom presentation suggests bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome as the nerve irritation is coming from past trauma to his wrists. This is causing the pain and tingling he was describing to me today.
2. Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including EMG testing to determine where nerve irritation is coming from. If these studies are positive for carpal tunnel syndrome we can consider referral to our hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery or refer him to an orthopedist for same treatment options.
3. Medical Treatment Plan: We will schedule an EMG test after which we can follow up with him if he is still having symptoms at that point we can consider referral to our hand clinic or orthopedist for further treatment options.

Allergies: Sulfa (causes rash).

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.

Eyes: Floaters.

She feels like this was less likely a true urinary tract infection and was just related to her constipation however we did have a good discussion regarding her leukocytosis.

• Constitutional: Reports fevers.

• Genitourinary: Reports dysuria.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney. She is a previously healthy child who was found to have a small kidney on one side. She reports that she was found to have a small kidney on one side when she was 4 years old. She was hospitalized 3-4 times for this, and she was treated with fluids and antibiotics. She denies hematuria.

She has been experiencing some stomach burning, and she reports hesitancy while urinating. She states that she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

The patient plays on softball team and is interested in joining a drill team over the summer.

PAST HISTORY

Family History: The patient's paternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves, obstructive neuropathy, end-stage chronic kidney disease, dialysis-dependent, failed renal transplant, and died of dialysis at age 47.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Pepcid 40 mg once daily.
Claritin as needed for allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard.
• Cardiovascular: Heart rate is regular in sinus rhythm. No murmurs or gallops heard.

RESULTS

Abdominal Ultrasound, 03/22/2021.
CT abdomen and pelvis, 03/22/2021.
CMP, 03/22/2021.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney. Her current symptoms include abdominal burning and hesitancy while urinating.
• Medical Reasoning: Her current symptoms are consistent with chronic pyelonephritis or possibly obstructive uropathy given her history of posterior urethral valves in her father's family history.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of staying hydrated during sports activities to prevent dehydration which can put tremendous strain on the kidneys. We also discussed the importance of maintaining a healthy diet to help keep her kidneys healthy as an adult.
• Medical Treatment: Continue Pepcid 40 mg once daily for dyspepsia symptoms. Continue Claritin as needed for allergies.
• Additional Testing: Annual ultrasound to monitor the size of her kidneys and their overall function; complete urinalysis to continue to make sure that protein and blood are not in her urine; blood pressure check every year.

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney. She is a previously healthy child who was found to have a small kidney on one side. She reports that she was found to have a small kidney on one side when she was 4 years old. She was hospitalized 3-4 times for this, and she was treated with fluids and antibiotics. She denies hematuria.

She has been experiencing some stomach burning, and she reports hesitancy while urinating. She states that she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

The patient plays on softball team and is interested in joining a drill team over the summer.

PAST HISTORY

Family History: The patient's paternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves, obstructive neuropathy, end-stage chronic kidney disease, dialysis-dependent, failed renal transplant, and died of dialysis at age 47.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Pepcid 40 mg once daily.
Claritin as needed for allergies.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard.
• Cardiovascular: Heart rate is regular in sinus rhythm. No murmurs or gallops heard.

RESULTS

Abdominal Ultrasound, 03/22/2021.
CT abdomen and pelvis, 03/22/2021.
CMP, 03/22/2021.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney. Her current symptoms include abdominal burning and hesitancy while urinating.
• Medical Reasoning: Her current symptoms are consistent with chronic pyelonephritis or possibly obstructive uropathy given her history of posterior urethral valves in her father's family history.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of staying hydrated during sports activities to prevent dehydration which can put tremendous strain on the kidneys. We also discussed the importance of maintaining a healthy diet to help keep her kidneys healthy as an adult.
• Medical Treatment: Continue Pepcid 40 mg once daily for dyspepsia symptoms. Continue Claritin as needed for allergies.
• Additional Testing: Annual ultrasound to monitor the size of her kidneys and their overall function; complete urinalysis to continue to make sure that protein and blood are not in her urine; blood pressure check every year.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily White is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 2 weeks ago. She reports that she has been having trouble reading and straight lines, as well as noticing that her door frames have been looking crooked to her. She also reports that she has trouble adjusting to dim lights when going out to dinner with her husband. She denies any pain with her eyes.

The patient is a smoker, smoking approximately 1 pack per day. She has tried to stop smoking on multiple occasions but has been unable to quit completely.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of macular degeneration.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking blood pressure medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Eyes: Reports blurred vision, difficulty adjusting to dim lights, and seeing door frames as crooked.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Examination of the anterior segment reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The right eye cornea is clear with no mVI or PCIOL cupping. The left eye cornea is clear with no mVII or PCIOL cupping. Cup-to-disc ratio is 0.2 in the right eye and 0.3 in the left eye. There are no signs of neovascularization or vitreous hemorrhage in either eye.
Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina attached 360 degrees without any tears or holes or posterior segment changes in the fovea. There are drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid and exudates accumulation positive for hemorrhage in the left eye. The left eye retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) shows drusen deposit, retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation, choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized.
Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's OCT results show drusen deposit, retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation, choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized which are consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Her fluorescein angiography results reveal focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular AMD.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for her current condition today including Lucentis injections once a month which may slow down vision decline or stop further vision loss but however disease progression may also occur despite treatment.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options for her current condition today including Lucentis injections once a month which may slow down vision decline or stop further vision loss but however disease progression may also occur despite treatment.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Price is a pleasant 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 1 day ago when she was participating in a mountain biking lesson. She was riding as a messenger and fell off her bike, twisting her right ankle outward. She reports that she heard a crack at the time of the injury. She has been taking Tylenol for pain, but it has not helped. She is limping and has been unable to bear weight on her right ankle. Her symptoms have been exacerbated by fever and chills.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she has been mountain biking for 3 years.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she has been taking Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain, swelling, and bruising. Denies numbness or tingling in her toes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Normal heart rate at 77 bpm, normal blood pressure at 118/77 mmHg, normal temperature at 98.6°C.
NEURO: Normal sensation to light touch in bilateral lower extremities.
MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals some edema and erythema on the lateral malleolus on the right hand side. There is associated ecchymosis and a few excoriations. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral malleolus. Decreased flexion and extension of the right ankle as well as internal and external rotation are present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right ankle sprain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical examination findings are consistent with an acute right ankle sprain.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including immobilization in an air cast, crutches, meloxicam 15 mg once daily, ice for 20 minutes 5 times daily, weight-bearing as tolerated, and follow-up in clinic if symptoms do not improve within 2 weeks.
- Medical Treatment: We have placed the patient in an air cast today. We have also prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily to help with pain control. We have also advised her to ice for 20 minutes 5 times daily and weight-bear as tolerated.
- Additional Testing: X-ray of the right foot was obtained today but not yet reviewed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

History of myocardial infarction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Garcia is a 72-year-old male who presents for a follow-up visit after he was treated for an inferior myocardial infarction. He was treated with stent placement in the right coronary artery. He reports that he is doing well, but he is still struggling and it was a scary time for him. He has been taking his medications as prescribed and has been doing light work at home. He denies any chest pain since the stent placement, but does report some soreness right after surgery that is improving. His wrist was red for a while, but it seems to be healing without infection. He reports shortness of breath when he walks up and down stairs.

The patient is a fan of the Denver Nuggets basketball team and enjoys swimming.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Myocardial infarction.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that he enjoys swimming.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention. No carotid bruits.
Cardiovascular: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Right radial artery cardiac cath site is clean, dry, and intact. There is no hematoma and there is a palpable radial pulse.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Ejection Fraction: approximately 50%.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Inferior myocardial infarction.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient had an inferior myocardial infarction with stent placement in the right coronary artery. His ejection fraction was approximately 50%. He has been taking his medications as prescribed and has been doing light work at home. We discussed the importance of continuing his medications to prevent re-occlusion of the stent or re-infarction.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including watching his salt intake, continuing to eat vegetables without salt, and avoiding excessive sodium intake from pizza on weekends.
- Medical Treatment: Continue aspirin lifelong until I tell you otherwise. Continue Brilinta for at least 1 year. Continue Crestor 40 mg once daily. Repeat echocardiogram in 6 months.
- Additional Testing: Liver function studies and lipid panel ordered to follow up with next visit in 6 weeks.

The patient reports that she does not watch the Super Bowl and therefore does not consume excessive amounts of junk food.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents for a routine check-up. He reports that he has been playing basketball for the first time in 2 years and when he went up for a rebound, he felt like his knee just popped. He started swelling and could hardly walk when it happened. He denies any previous history of right knee pain.

The patient reports that his pain is located on the inside of his right knee. He is able to bear weight on that leg but favors it for sure. His pain is described as achy. The patient has tried Tylenol, which has provided some relief but not much. His pain level is approximately 4 out of 10.

The patient notes that his swelling has decreased since he slept overnight. He denies any other symptoms such as redness or warmth around the area.

Regarding his hypertension, the patient reports that his blood pressure has been in the 140-150/80 range today. He notes that he takes Norvasc 5 mg daily and is compliant with this medication. His blood pressure was elevated at today’s visit, however, we discussed changing his medication to try to get this down.

The patient reports that he eats anything he wants and denies any dietary changes recently.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Reports gastrointestinal upset with metformin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the left sternal border bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee shows no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right knee MCL strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury while playing basketball and presents with right knee pain, swelling, ecchymosis, and limited range of motion. X-ray of the right knee shows no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continued use of Tylenol for pain management, prescription for meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain management and swelling reduction, placement in a right knee immobilizer for 2 weeks, and MRI to confirm MCL strain or tear.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Tylenol as needed for pain management only. Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain management and swelling reduction. Place in a right knee immobilizer for 2 weeks. Obtain MRI to confirm MCL strain or tear.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s blood pressure was elevated at today’s visit despite compliance with Norvasc 5 mg daily.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including changing his medication to try to get his blood pressure down to <120/80 mmHg.
- Medical Treatment: Increase Norvasc from 5 mg daily to 10 mg daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated and fluctuating blood pressures.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Robert Harris is a 67-year-old male with a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis who presents today for the evaluation of elevated and fluctuating blood pressures. The patient reports that his blood pressure has been well controlled over the last 3 to 4 weeks, but he has experienced periods of lightheadedness, slight headache, and elevated upper numbers on blood pressure checks. He denies any chest pain or respiratory symptoms. The patient also reports experiencing dizziness with unsteady gait and mild headaches when his blood pressure numbers have been higher.

The patient is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg twice per day, atorvastatin, and occasional Tylenol. He denies missing doses of his medication. The patient has used a pill box and then tried an app to help him keep track of his medication schedule. He is currently using the app.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys playing golf.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 20 mg twice per day.
Atorvastatin.
Occasional Tylenol.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior examination. No murmurs or gallops heard at the apex or pulmonary area. No signs of heart failure or valvular disease.
Respiratory: Mild bibasilar rales bilaterally without wheezes or rhonchi. Excellent air movement in all lung fields. No wheezes or rhonchi heard at the lungs bilaterally.
Neurological: Trace lower extremity edema bilaterally otherwise normal examination.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Elevated Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure readings have been fluctuating over the past few weeks with episodes of lightheadedness and headaches when his upper numbers are elevated. His current medication regimen includes lisinopril 20 mg twice per day which was increased from once per day at our last visit but he still experiences elevated readings on occasion.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including increasing fluid intake to stay hydrated as well as limiting alcohol consumption to no more than 2 drinks per week.
- Medical Treatment: We will increase his lisinopril to 60 mg twice per day in addition to adding hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily which should help even out his readings. I want him to check his blood pressure twice daily for the next two weeks before we see him again in two weeks for follow-up.
2. Hyperlipidemia.
- Medical Reasoning: His current lipid panel was not provided but he is doing well on atorvastatin which should continue to be continued as prescribed by me today in addition to sending a cholesterol panel along with a CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, and urinalysis for further evaluation of kidney function.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including diet changes that can help lower cholesterol levels such as reducing saturated fat intake and increasing soluble fiber intake from foods such as oats, barley, fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, etc., along with regular exercise such as brisk walking for at least most days of the week.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current management with atorvastatin as prescribed today in addition to sending additional lab tests for further evaluation of kidney function.
3. Osteoarthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is still able to walk full courses when he can but there are times when weather changes cause him to play less or skip a day altogether due to pain in his knees which he treats with Tylenol for mild pain when needed and modifies activity accordingly when symptoms occur.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Billy Wright is a 74-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a cough. The patient reports that he started coughing about a week ago. He has been bringing up some yellow stuff and not feeling well for the last 2 days. He denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, runny nose, sore throat, or sinus pressure.

The patient reports that he was coughing and fell down the stairs this morning. He states that he twisted his right knee when he fell. He denies any pain in his left knee. The patient reports that he can bend and straighten his right knee but it hurts mostly on the inside when he walks. He denies limping.

The patient reports that he has not been taking his blood sugars or monitoring his diet for diabetes.

PAST HISTORY

History of hypertension.
History of diabetes.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 20 mg daily.
Metformin 1000 mg twice a day.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Examination of the respiratory system reveals erythema and edema of the nasal turbinates bilaterally with associated yellow discharge. There is no erythema or exudate in the peritonsillar space on throat exam. Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough.
Cardiovascular: Examination of the cardiovascular system reveals a regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the musculoskeletal system reveals pain to palpation over the right knee. Decreased flexion and extension of the right knee with associated ecchymosis to the right medial knee. No evidence of effusion.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Prior results are available on file.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cough.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of a cough which began approximately 1 week ago. His symptoms have worsened over time, however, he denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, runny nose, sore throat or sinus pressure.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him today that I believe he has a viral syndrome at this time and possibly mild bronchitis. I recommended supportive care including guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help cough up phlegm as well as over-the-counter medications for symptom relief.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue to monitor his symptoms at home today and if they worsen we will consider ordering a chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia.
2. Right Knee Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of right knee pain which began approximately 1 hour ago after falling down stairs while coughing this morning. He denies any left knee pain or limping at this time but does report some pain when walking on his right side due to decreased flexion and extension in this joint with associated ecchymosis to the medial aspect of this joint without effusion present on examination today.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him today that I believe he has sustained a right medial collateral ligament strain from his fall this morning and we will refer him to physical therapy to help strengthen muscles around this area as well as order an x-ray to rule out any bony injury at this time.
- Medical Treatment: We will prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management at home today as well as refer him to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around his right knee joint.

She also reports dizziness and blurry vision when she has headaches. The patient denies chest pain or shortness of breath when she experiences headaches. She reports that Tylenol helps with her headaches.

The patient also reports that she is taking metformin for diabetes and denies taking it as prescribed, stating that she takes it every other day. She reports that her blood sugar levels have been elevated lately, including this morning when her fasting blood sugar.

The patient denies any nausea or vomiting associated with her headaches or elevated blood sugar levels.

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain and shortness of breath.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Theresa Rodriguez is a 41-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of high blood pressure and elevated blood sugar levels.
• Medical Reasoning:
The patient's symptoms are consistent with uncontrolled hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2. Her current medication regimen is suboptimal due to non-adherence to prescribed dosing schedule and dietary habits are likely contributing factors to her elevated blood pressure and glucose levels.
• Patient Education and Counseling:
The patient will be counseled in regards to lifestyle modifications including dietary changes to reduce sodium intake, increased physical activity, stress reduction techniques, and smoking cessation if applicable. We will also discuss alternative sources of protein such as fish which may be lower in sodium than fast food options like McDonald’s.
The patient will also be counseled on how to properly take her medications including chlorthalidone and metformin daily without missing doses.
• Medical Treatment:
The patient will continue with chlorthalidone daily as prescribed today but we will monitor her blood pressure three times per week at home using a home blood pressure monitor provided by the office. We will also increase her metformin dose to 1500 mg daily as prescribed today in an attempt to improve glycemic control while continuing regular monitoring of her glucose levels at home as well.

Chronic lumbar back pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sharon Wright is a 36-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right shoulder pain. The onset of her symptoms began 3 weeks ago when she was painting and fell while reaching out. She states that she braced herself but did not fall. She denies any pre-existing right shoulder pain.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing right shoulder pain, which is constant but intermittent, and is worse with lifting overhead and raising her arm overhead. She rates her pain level as a 6 without any Tylenol or Advil, and as a 4 when taking Tylenol or Advil. The patient reports that her pain improves with medication.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in her arm or hand at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right shoulder pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No tenderness to palpation over the sternoclavicular joint.
Right Shoulder: Limited active and passive range of motion. Tenderness to palpation over the greater tuberosity of the humerus. Good strong bilateral hand grip strength.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right shoulder reveals no fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right rotator cuff tendinopathy.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy, which is consistent with her history of direct trauma to the area.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today, including physical therapy and steroid injections if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an MRI of the right shoulder to rule out any other pathology. I have referred her to physical therapy for 6-8 weeks at this time. If she does not improve, we will discuss additional treatment options such as steroid injections.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Vision changes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Thomas is a 65-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of vision changes. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 to 4 months ago. He reports that he has trouble adjusting in dark environments, particularly when reading. He also notes that straight lines appear wavy to him, which he attributes to the paneling in his office. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient reports that he and his wife dine out almost every night and he believes that this may be contributing to his vision problems. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes daily and reports that he has tried various methods to quit including hypnosis, lozenges, and chewing gum. He admits to occasionally smoking without his wife present.

PAST HISTORY

History of high blood pressure.
Smoking 1 pack of cigarettes daily.

MEDICATIONS

Blood pressure medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Eyes: Reports vision changes, difficulty adjusting in dark environments, straight lines appear wavy to him.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Examination of the anterior segment reveals clear corneas with no signs of nVI or peak hole. Cupping is 2mm. Fundus examination reveals retinal detachment at 360 degrees in the right eye with no holes or tears noted. RPE changes are present in the fovea. Drusen are present under the RPE bilaterally with retinal thickening and subretinal fluid accumulation and exudate accumulation bilaterally. There is a hemorrhage present in the right eye bilaterally there is no subretinal fluid or hemorrhage noted.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Diagnostic exam shows drusen deposits under the RPE which is the retinal pigment epithelium and then subretinal fluid so SRF accumulation and choroidal neovascular membrane can also be visualized in that test.
Fluorescein angiography shows focal area of leakage consistent with neurovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Matthew Thomas is a 65-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of vision changes.
Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (wet macular degeneration) is diagnosed based on diagnostic exam findings and fluorescein angiography results today.
Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms have been progressive over the past 3-4 months, which suggests an advanced stage of wet macular degeneration. His last injection was performed approximately 1 month ago, which may have contributed to his current worsening symptoms.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for wet macular degeneration today including intravitreal injections with Lucentis once per month. I explained that these injections can help slow down vision loss but may not completely stop it. I also explained that there may still be some vision loss after treatment but this will be minimal compared to if we had not treated at all.
Medical Treatment: We will start Lucentis injections once per month starting immediately today at our clinic today after numbing the eye so you will not feel any pain during injection at all patients report no pain at all for actual injection today we will also provide him with a prescription for blood pressure medication as prescribed as well as instructions on how to check his blood pressure regularly.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee contusion.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Joe Reed is a 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain and swelling. The onset of his symptoms began on Saturday when he was skiing at Mount Saint Helen and Washington. He was skiing down a mountain when he lost control and did a cartwheel, but stopped halfway through. He felt a pop in his right knee and experienced immediate pain. He has been taking Advil and icing his knee on and off since then, as well as applying heat occasionally. He denies any previous knee injuries.

The patient reports that he has been able to walk, but it is definitely swollen and painful. He denies any previous shoulder injuries.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any neurological symptoms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: Vital signs are stable today. No fever, 97.9 degrees F, heart rate 64 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98%.
Musculoskeletal Examination: Examination of the right knee reveals edema and ecchymosis around the surrounding area. Positive pain to palpation over the medial aspect of the right knee with flexion and extension. Range of motion is full but feels tight with pain upon movement.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee shows no fracture or bony abnormalities.
X-ray of the right shoulder shows no fracture or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee contusion.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained a right knee contusion while skiing on Saturday. His symptoms have not improved with rest, ice, Advil, and icing his knee on and off since then.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for his current symptoms in detail today.
- Medical Treatment: We will need to rest that apply ice 2-3 times a day for 20 minutes at a time take some NSAIDs or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication such as ibuprofen every 6-8 hours as needed if that does not improve then we can go ahead and maybe come back in and we might do some physical therapy as well.
- Additional Testing: X-ray of the right shoulder will be ordered due to bruising in that area.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up on stage III non-small cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up on her stage III non-small cell lung cancer. She has been taking mile-long walks with her Doberman. She is currently taking cisplatin and etoposide chemotherapy. Her husband is her support system, and her daughter has also been helpful.

The patient reports that she has noticed shortness of breath over the weekend. She states that she was previously active and would walk around the block, but now she can only walk down the street without being short of breath. The patient denies coughing or phlegm. She also denies fever. The patient reports that she has a dry cough, which hurts when she swallows. She denies food getting stuck when swallowing. The patient states that she has not been taking hydrocortisone liquids as much because it hurts so much, but she is able to drink Ensure and milkshakes.

On mental/emotional status, the patient reports that she is devastated by her diagnosis and is trying to figure everything out. She states that her husband and daughter are very helpful and supportive.

The patient reports that she was a little nauseated and tired from chemotherapy, but took Zofran which seemed to help. She got some rest and it has been okay.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports being active with mile-long walks with her Doberman.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs.
Lungs: Bilateral crackles bilaterally due to fluid in the lungs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Stage III non-small cell lung cancer.
- Continue cisplatin and etoposide chemotherapy.
- Continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy.
- Obtain additional testing after completion of current radiation regimen to evaluate for surgical resection of tumor.
2. Radiation pneumonitis.
- Prescribe low dose steroid prednisone 40 mg once daily for 5 days to reduce inflammation in the lungs.
- Patient denies prior steroid use; advised that this should not cause significant side effects due to short duration of treatment.
3. Dysphagia due to esophageal inflammation from radiation pneumonitis.
- Prescribe lidocaine lozenges 4 times daily to help with pain-free swallowing.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago. The patient describes the pain as starting in his right flank and radiating down to his groin. He states that the pain is usually under control, but he has had episodes where it gets a little out of control. He notes that his symptoms are worse with increased fluid intake and strenuous activity. The patient denies any hematuria or dysuria. He does report a history of right testicular pain, which resolved with some relief.

The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for his pain, which has provided some relief but not complete resolution. His pain score is approximately 4/10 when it is more severe and 1-2/10 when it is less severe.

The patient reports that he has had kidney stones in the past, including some that he was able to pass on his own within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy. He also notes that there is a significant family history of kidney stones.

PAST HISTORY

Personal history of kidney stones, some passed independently, usually within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy.
Significant family history of kidney stones.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Constitutional: Notably elevated blood pressure.
• Cardiovascular: No murmurs or gallops.
• Respiratory: No wheezes or rales.
• Gastrointestinal: No abdominal tenderness to palpation in all quadrants. CVA tenderness over the right side of the abdomen due to kidney stone.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of the right flank was reviewed today, 05/06/2022. It revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's CT scan from today confirms a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size located on the proximal right ureter without evidence of hydronephrosis.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with him today and he understands what we discussed at length.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
Medical Treatment Plan:
- Continue pushing fluids to try to pass the stone.
- Continue ibuprofen as needed for pain control.
- Prescription for tramadol 50 mg as needed for breakthrough pain if ibuprofen does not provide adequate relief.
- Continue using strainer whenever urinating to try to catch any passing stone fragments.
- Order BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to evaluate for infection and assess if antibiotics are needed at this time.
- Schedule follow-up appointment in 1-2 weeks if symptoms persist.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Frank Lee is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago. He reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath when walking up stairs and walking quickly. He denies any exertional dyspnea at rest. He does report that he has been urinating at night, but this has been present for some time.

The patient reports that he had a similar episode 6 months ago, which resolved with an increase in his Lasix dose. He notes that he has been watching his salt intake since then and believes that this was the cause of his improvement.

The patient reports that he has stage 3 chronic kidney disease and notes that he is currently taking Lasix 40 mg once daily. He denies any swelling in his legs.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, and placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018. He also reports a history of knee pain.

MEDICATIONS

The patient is currently taking Lasix 40 mg once daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies hemoptysis, productive cough, or dyspnea on exertion at rest.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or palpitations.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports knee pain.
• Neurological: Denies weakness or numbness in the extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: JVD up to 9 cm bilaterally present. No carotid bruits.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Chest X-ray ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute heart failure exacerbation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with an acute heart failure exacerbation given his history of coronary disease and current symptoms of shortness of breath at rest and with exertion. His elevated blood pressure is also consistent with this diagnosis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the importance of increasing his Lasix dose to 80 mg once daily to help manage his fluid overload and improve his symptoms. I also advised him to call me if he experiences worsening shortness of breath before starting the increased dose.
- Medical Treatment: We will increase his Lasix dose to 80 mg once daily starting today. We will also order a chest x-ray to rule out any other causes for his current symptoms.
2. Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's echocardiogram from last year showed decreased ejection fraction, which is consistent with coronary artery disease.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the importance of continuing to follow up with Dr White as we have previously discussed regarding his coronary artery disease.
- Medical Treatment: We will order another echocardiogram to check on the status of his heart murmur from last year as well as confirm that there is no worsening ejection fraction.
3. Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with possible gout given his history of chronic kidney disease and current foot pain which resolved after taking Motrin for several days but returned after stopping it. His elevated potassium levels could also be contributing to his current symptoms as well as gout flare-up due to high potassium intake from diet high in bananas, oranges, potatoes etc., which can cause kidney dysfunction due to inability to excrete potassium properly due to decreased renal function.
